liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Reviewer wonders whether this Scarlet Begonias is one of the best ever played; Reviewer finds Jerry uninspired, off in places, playing wrong-scale notes, and giving little jam leadership; the jam fades away [18][21]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer, usually lukewarm on Jack Straw, found this version fierce, passionate and almost frightening [22]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer finds this Fire on the Mountain completely surreal [20]
- **From The Heart Of Me** (1 review): Reviewer usually dislikes this song but rated this version a standout [12]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Reviewer recommends the Not Fade Away into Mojo jam as a funky highlight of the show [16]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 other source): Johnny B. Goode was the encore [1]
- **Caution Jam** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Caution into Mojo jam as the best part of the show [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-10-22.sonyecm280.martin-bunton.102076.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 188 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1978-10-22.sonyecm280.martin-bunton.102077.flac24**: source not stated; 21 songs; 188 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd78-10-22.sbd.kempa.299.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 176 min; rated 4.61/5 by 18 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this Fire sounds three-dimensional, as if extra speakers sit behind the listener, perhaps due to miking and panning; Reviewer praises the mix and sound, saying this tape differs from most and may be better [14][16]
- **gd1978-10-22.sbd.nugs.21247.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 176 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [4]
- **gd1978-10-22.mtx.seamons.99496.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 179 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Bill Graham and Mickey Hart [1]
- Reviewer calls the first set excellent and the second set, especially after drums, incandescent [13]
- Reviewer, at their third show, recalls colorful dragons in red, silver and blue, and Winterland's cave-like interior [15]
- Reviewer notes that Donna was in tune at this show [16]
- Reviewer's brother attended this run of Winterland shows and later asked them to find tapes of them [17]
- Hamza El Din joined on Ollin Arrageed, and Lee Oskar sat in during Drums [1]
- John Cippolina played guitar from Not Fade Away through Goin' Down The Road Feelin' Bad [1]
- Hamza El Din played solo until the band joined in on Ollin Arageed; Lee Oskar played harmonica during Drums [4]
- John Cipollina played guitar from Not Fade Away through Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad [4]
- Reviewer prefers the Scarlet Begonias from Fox Atlanta, 11/30/80, as a truly inspired one [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-10-22.sonyecm280.martin-bunton.102076.flac16**: taped by Mike Martin and Mark Bunton; transferred by Mike Martin; source: 2 Sony ecm-280 microphones (shoulder high) > Teac PC-10 w/ Dolby > TDK SA-C90 tape. Our location was on the floor under the mirrored ball about 20-25 feet from… [1]
- **gd1978-10-22.sonyecm280.martin-bunton.102077.flac24**: taped by Mike Martin and Mark Bunton; transferred by Mike Martin; source: Two Sony ecm-280 microphones (shoulder high) > Teac PC-10 w/ Dolby > TDK SA-C90 tape [2]. Also: The tape was flipped during Olin Arageed and the two pieces were spliced together; A microphone became unplugged during Olin Arageed, so a pseudo-stereo mix was created for part of that track; Fifty-nine distracting out-of-sync claps were deleted from the first disc's fourth track [2]
- **gd78-10-22.sbd.kempa.299.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1978-10-22.sbd.nugs.21247.flac16**: transferred by nugs.net; source: SBD>Master Reel>Cassette>DAT>WAV [4]. Also: All five October 1978 Winterland shows come from soundboard sources of varying quality, with splices and cassette-flip cuts [4]
- **gd1978-10-22.mtx.seamons.99496.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [5]. Also: Soundboard went to Maxell UDXL-I cassette master, then PCM, Sony R500, Peak, Samplitude and FLAC; transfers and mastering by Charlie Miller; Audience source: two AKG d224e microphones into a Sony TC 158, onto Maxell UDXL II cassettes, then preserved via Nakamichi CR7a and Korg MR-1000 [5]
